label: early copy steps (outputting orig 1-2) of long sequences, specific input tokens, w/z upcoming
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost entirely at the second and third output steps (recall_idx 1: 33% of mass, recall_idx 2: 64%; a little at 3; never at the delimiter or in the original phase). Activity rises with L (L>=7 gives most of the mass). Within that window it is sparse (about 3% of eligible steps) and depends jointly on the token being fed back (in_tok, i.e. orig(0) or orig(1); n, 0, f, z, 1, c, q, e, w are enriched) and on the token being output now or next (w is by far the strongest, about 12x lift, then z, s, l). The largest activations are at recall_idx 2 with input orig(1) from that set while w/z is being output or coming next (e.g. j n z w ... <DEL> j [n]). Window plus input-token set alone covers about 81% of mass but at 12% precision; adding the output/next-token condition raises precision to about 41% but cuts mass recall to about 48%. Best dev F1 is about 0.39, so it reads as a conjunctive position x input-token x upcoming-token code that one predicate does not capture cleanly.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=n (+3.76), orig2=w (+3.74), orig3=w (+3.61), phase=2 & in_tok=z (+3.39), phase=2 & out_tok=z (+3.05), orig1=w (+3.00). Lower it: to_go=1 (-5.91), in_first=1 (-4.29), to_go=0 (-4.09), next_out=- (-3.84).
